title: Diversity-Oriented Organizational Development in Emergency Care
summary:
The diversity of healthcare staff and patients in emergency departments with particularly challenging structural conditions is increasing. However, it remains unclear how characteristics of patients—such as gender, body weight, and migration history—influence the care of abdominal pain. ED-DIVERSE aims to improve workflows and treatments in ways that relieve emergency department teams and ensure the best possible care for all patients.

Specifically, the project seeks to:

1. Identify social mechanisms and structures in emergency departments that contribute to unequal care related to patient characteristics such as gender, body weight, and migration history (current situation),

and, based on these findings,

2. Develop approaches to diversity-sensitive emergency care together with healthcare staff and patients (target situation). These approaches are designed to build on existing workflows and processes.

To achieve these goals, the project uses a research approach that combines different methods (mixed-methods design) in five emergency departments in Berlin. This includes a patient survey, observations of everyday work in the emergency department, and in-depth interviews. In follow-up workshops with managerial and non-managerial healthcare staff as well as representatives of patient and self-help groups, practical recommendations are developed. These recommendations will feed into setting-specific concepts for diversity-oriented organizational development in emergency departments.
conditions: Intersectional inequitable treatment of non-traumatic abdominal pain (NTAP) based on gender, (ascribed) ethnic affiliation, and/or overweight/obesity

interventions.name: A survey of n=576 patients presenting with the chief complaint of abdominal pain assessing experiences of discrimination based on gender, migration background, or increased body weight; barriers to access to and utilisation of healthcare services prior to the emergency department visit; duration and

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with abdominal pain:
- Treated during the study period in the participating emergency departments
- Presentation to the emergency department with abdominal pain
- Ability to provide informed consent (personally or via legal representative)
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with abdominal pain:
- Obvious trauma or accident as the cause of the abdominal pain
- Presence of a positive shock index upon admission to the emergency department
- Insufficient proficiency in any of the 5 available languages (German, Turkish, Arabic, Russian, English) to participate
- Private health insurance
